offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Nonperson Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant operated or attempted to operate a vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs to a degree that rendered the person incapable of safely driving
Or with a BAC of .08 or higher
Or while there was any amount of a controlled substance in the person's blood or urine
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours imprisonment or 100 hours community service (first); 90 days (second); 90 days (third); 90 days (fourth+)
enhancements: Second offense within 10 years (Class A Misdemeanor)
Fourth or subsequent (Nonperson Felony, severity level 6)
notes: Kansas uses a lookback period — prior convictions within lifetime count for enhancement after 2012 changes. Implied consent under K.S.A. § 8-1001. License suspension 30 days + 330 days restricted (first).

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
BAC .08 or higher, or impairment shown
No prior DUI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours imprisonment or 100 hours community service; completion of alcohol evaluation; license suspension 30 days + 330 days ignition interlock
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (additional mandatory minimum of 48 hours)
notes: First offense with standard evaluation and compliance. Diversion may be available for first-time offenders in some jurisdictions.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (second); Nonperson Felony (third+)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle while under the influence
Defendant has one or more prior DUI convictions or diversions
mandatory_minimum: 90 days imprisonment (second+); cannot be reduced below 90 days (third+); mandatory treatment program
notes: Third and subsequent DUIs are felonies in Kansas. 90-day mandatory minimum cannot be reduced for third+. License revocation 1 year (second), 1 year (third+). Prior diversions count as convictions.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle
While under the influence of any drug or combination of drugs to a degree that rendered the person incapable of safely driving
Or with any amount of a controlled substance or its metabolite in blood or urine
notes: Kansas has a per se drug DUI provision — any detectable amount of a controlled substance in blood or urine is sufficient for conviction. Includes marijuana metabolites. No impairment showing needed for per se violation.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second+)
elements: Defendant drove a vehicle on any highway
In willful or wanton disregard for the safety of persons or property
enhancements: Second or subsequent conviction (Class A Misdemeanor)
notes: Kansas has a mandatory minimum for reckless driving. Commonly used as a plea reduction from DUI charges.

statute_title: Duty to Stop at Accident — Leaving the Scene
offense_class: Person Felony severity level 9 (injury); Class B Misdemeanor (property only)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Resulting in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop, provide information, or render aid
enhancements: Great bodily harm or death (Person Felony severity level 7)
notes: Leaving scene with injury is a person felony — sentencing follows Kansas sentencing guidelines grid. Property damage only is a Class B Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 4
penalty_max: Presumptive guidelines — typically 38-172 months depending on criminal history
elements: Defendant unintentionally killed a human being
While committing, attempting, or fleeing from a DUI offense
enhancements: Criminal history elevates sentence on guidelines grid
notes: Kansas charges DUI-related vehicular deaths as involuntary manslaughter under § 21-5405(a)(3). Severity level 4 person felony — one of the most serious vehicular offenses. Sentencing follows the Kansas Sentencing Guidelines grid.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5
penalty_max: Presumptive guidelines — typically 31-136 months depending on criminal history
elements: Defendant unintentionally killed a human being
While committing a lawful act in an unlawful manner
Or while committing an unlawful act not amounting to a felony
notes: Non-DUI vehicular deaths caused by reckless or negligent driving. Lower severity level than DUI involuntary manslaughter.

statute_title: Driving While Suspended, Cancelled, or Revoked
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Nonperson Felony severity level 9 (third+)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on a highway
While driving privilege was cancelled, suspended, or revoked
enhancements: Second offense (Class A Misdemeanor with 90-day mandatory)
Third or subsequent (Nonperson Felony severity level 9)
notes: Mandatory minimum jail for all offenses. Third offense becomes a felony. Habitual violator provisions may apply.

statute_title: Fleeing or Attempting to Elude a Police Officer
offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 9 (vehicle); Class B Misdemeanor (on foot)
elements: Defendant, while driving a motor vehicle
Willfully failed or refused to bring the vehicle to a stop
Or otherwise fled or attempted to elude a pursuing police vehicle
When given visual or audible signal to stop
enhancements: Committed in a reckless manner — at least 5 mph over limit, driving through a residential zone, or causing property damage (Person Felony severity level 9)
Resulting in bodily harm (Person Felony severity level 7)
notes: Felony when using a vehicle. Becomes a person felony when committed recklessly. Kansas sentencing guidelines apply.

offense_class: Drug severity level 5 (most substances); Drug severity level 4 (cocaine, heroin, meth); Drug severity level 3 (large amounts)
penalty_max: Per drug sentencing guidelines grid — typically 10-42 months depending on history and severity
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
Without a valid prescription
notes: Kansas has a separate drug sentencing guidelines grid. Possession of opiates, cocaine, and meth is a higher drug severity level. Mandatory drug abuse treatment for first-time offenders under SB 123.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Drug severity level 5 (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed marijuana or tetrahydrocannabinol
notes: Kansas has not legalized marijuana. First possession is a Class B Misdemeanor — one of the lowest penalties. Third offense becomes a felony on the drug grid. Possession of paraphernalia is a separate charge.

offense_class: Drug severity level 5 (first); Drug severity level 4 (subsequent or 3.5g+)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
enhancements: Amount of 3.5 grams or more (Drug severity level 4)
notes: Cocaine possession is a drug severity level 5 felony. Sentencing follows the Kansas drug sentencing guidelines grid. SB 123 treatment provisions may apply for first offenders.

offense_class: Drug severity level 5 (first); Drug severity level 4 (subsequent or 3.5g+)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
enhancements: Amount of 3.5 grams or more (Drug severity level 4)
notes: Same severity level as cocaine. Meth is a significant enforcement priority in Kansas. SB 123 treatment program may apply for eligible first offenders.

statute_title: Sale or Distribution of Controlled Substance — Trafficking Amounts
offense_class: Drug severity level 1 (largest amounts); Drug severity level 2 (large amounts)
penalty_max: Per drug sentencing guidelines — up to 204 months for level 1 with criminal history
elements: Defendant knowingly sold, offered for sale, or possessed with intent to sell a controlled substance
In amounts exceeding statutory trafficking thresholds
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory imprisonment — no probation for drug severity level 1 or 2
enhancements: Proximity to school (additional consecutive term under § 21-5710)
notes: Kansas drug trafficking carries the highest drug severity levels. No probation available. Sentencing follows the drug grid with mandatory prison terms.

statute_title: Sale or Distribution of a Controlled Substance
offense_class: Drug severity level 3 (Schedule I/II); Drug severity level 4 (Schedule III/IV)
elements: Defendant knowingly sold, offered for sale, or distributed a controlled substance
Or possessed with intent to sell or distribute
enhancements: Within 1,000 feet of school property (additional consecutive term under § 21-5710)
notes: Distribution covers smaller amounts than trafficking. Drug severity level depends on the schedule of the substance.

offense_class: Drug severity level 1 (meth); Drug severity level 2 (other Schedule I/II)
penalty_max: Per drug sentencing guidelines — up to 204 months (level 1)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured or attempted to manufacture a controlled substance
notes: Meth manufacturing is drug severity level 1 — the highest level on the drug grid. No probation available. Includes possession of precursors with intent to manufacture.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (marijuana paraphernalia); Drug severity level 5 (other substance paraphernalia, if possession with intent to use)
penalty_max: 1 year (Class A); per drug grid (drug severity level 5)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed drug paraphernalia
With intent to use to introduce a controlled substance into the body
notes: Marijuana paraphernalia possession is a Class A Misdemeanor. Paraphernalia associated with harder drugs may be charged at a higher severity level.

offense_class: Drug severity level 3 (Schedule I/II); Drug severity level 4 (Schedule III/IV/V)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
With intent to sell, distribute, or deliver
notes: Intent inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, large cash, and other circumstantial evidence. Charged under the distribution statute.

offense_class: Off-grid Person Felony
penalty_min: 25 years (Hard 25) or 50 years (Hard 50) before parole eligibility
elements: Defendant intentionally and with premeditation killed a human being
Or killed a human being in the commission of, attempt to commit, or flight from an inherently dangerous felony
mandatory_minimum: Hard 25 — 25 years minimum before parole eligibility; Hard 50 for certain aggravated cases
enhancements: Hard 50 sentencing for specified aggravating factors (K.S.A. § 21-6620)
notes: Kansas abolished the death penalty in practice via judicial interpretation, reinstated it, and currently has it on the books but no executions since 1965. First-degree murder is an off-grid felony — not on the sentencing guidelines grid. Hard 25 or Hard 50 minimum.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 1 (intentional); Person Felony, severity level 2 (unintentional but reckless)
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — up to 653 months (severity level 1 with criminal history)
elements: Defendant intentionally killed a human being (without premeditation)
Or unintentionally killed while committing an act clearly dangerous to human life under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to human life
notes: Intentional second-degree murder (no premeditation) is severity level 1. Reckless/depraved-heart murder is severity level 2. Both follow the sentencing guidelines grid.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 3
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — up to 247 months with criminal history
elements: Defendant knowingly killed a human being
Upon a sudden quarrel or in the heat of passion
notes: Heat of passion must result from adequate provocation. Cannot claim imperfect self-defense in Kansas — this is the primary voluntary manslaughter theory.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5 (general); severity level 4 (DUI-related)
elements: Defendant unintentionally killed a human being
During the commission of a lawful act in an unlawful manner
Or during the commission of an unlawful act not amounting to a felony
notes: Involuntary manslaughter while DUI is severity level 4 — significantly higher than general involuntary manslaughter (level 5). Sentencing follows Kansas guidelines grid.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 7
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — typically 11-34 months depending on criminal history
elements: Defendant knowingly placed another person in reasonable apprehension of immediate bodily harm
While using a deadly weapon
Or while disguised
notes: Aggravated assault requires a deadly weapon or disguise. Person felony — affects criminal history score for future offenses. Kansas distinguishes assault (threat) from battery (contact).

offense_class: Class C Person Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly placed another person in reasonable apprehension of immediate bodily harm
enhancements: With a deadly weapon or while disguised (Aggravated Assault — felony)
notes: Simple assault in Kansas is only a threat — no physical contact. Class C person misdemeanor is the lowest level. Contact offenses are 'battery' in Kansas.

offense_class: Class B Person Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused bodily harm to another person
Or caused physical contact with another person in a rude, insulting, or angry manner
enhancements: Against a law enforcement officer (Class A Person Misdemeanor)
notes: Battery is the physical contact offense in Kansas. Assault is the threat-only offense. Important distinction for charging purposes.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — typically 31-136 months depending on criminal history
elements: Defendant took property from the person or presence of another
By threat of bodily harm or by force
enhancements: Use of deadly weapon or infliction of bodily harm (Aggravated Robbery — severity level 3)
notes: Robbery requires force or threat of force. Taking without force is theft. Person felony affects future criminal history scoring.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 3
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — up to 247 months with criminal history
elements: Defendant committed robbery
While armed with a dangerous weapon
Or while inflicting bodily harm upon any person
notes: Aggravated robbery is severity level 3 — the same level as voluntary manslaughter. Sentencing follows the guidelines grid.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5 (kidnapping); Off-grid Person Felony (aggravated kidnapping — bodily harm to extort)
elements: Defendant took or confined any person by force, threat, or deception
With intent to hold for ransom, as a shield/hostage, to facilitate a crime, or to inflict bodily injury or terrorize
mandatory_minimum: Hard 20 or Hard 25 for aggravated kidnapping
notes: Aggravated kidnapping is an off-grid person felony with Hard 20 or Hard 25 minimum before parole. Regular kidnapping is severity level 5 on the grid.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 6 (arson); Person Felony, severity level 3 (aggravated arson — occupied building)
elements: Defendant knowingly, by means of fire or explosive, damaged or destroyed property
With intent to injure or defraud an insurer or another person
enhancements: Occupied building or structure (Aggravated Arson — severity level 3)
notes: Arson is a nonperson felony unless the building is occupied. Aggravated arson (occupied) is a person felony severity level 3 — extremely serious.

offense_class: Off-grid Person Felony
elements: Defendant, with intent to commit first-degree murder, performed an overt act toward the commission of murder
That was more than mere preparation
notes: Attempted first-degree murder is an off-grid person felony in Kansas. The Hard 20 minimum applies. Attempted second-degree murder follows the sentencing grid.

statute_title: Aggravated Battery — With a Deadly Weapon
offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 4
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — typically 38-172 months depending on criminal history
elements: Defendant knowingly caused bodily harm to another person
With a deadly weapon
Or in a manner that could have caused great bodily harm, disfigurement, or death
notes: Kansas calls this aggravated battery when physical contact occurs. Aggravated assault with a deadly weapon (threat only, no contact) is severity level 7.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,500); Nonperson Felony, severity level 9 ($1,500-$24,999); severity level 7 ($25,000-$99,999); severity level 5 ($100,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exerted unauthorized control over property of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Theft of a firearm (severity level 9 regardless of value)
notes: Kansas unified theft statute. Felony threshold is $1,500. Theft of a firearm is automatically a severity level 9 nonperson felony. Sentencing follows Kansas guidelines.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 9 ($1,500-$24,999); level 7 ($25,000-$99,999); level 5 ($100,000+)
elements: Defendant obtained or exerted unauthorized control over property
With intent to permanently deprive
Value $1,500 or more
notes: Kansas does not use 'grand theft' terminology. Felony theft at various severity levels based on property value.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant obtained or exerted unauthorized control over property
With intent to permanently deprive
Value under $1,500
notes: Misdemeanor theft covers property valued under $1,500. Kansas has a relatively high felony threshold compared to many states.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (under $1,500); Nonperson Felony (severity level 9 for $1,500+)
elements: Defendant obtained or exerted unauthorized control over merchandise from a retail establishment
With intent to permanently deprive the retailer
notes: Shoplifting is charged under the general theft statute. Civil recovery may also be pursued by the retailer.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 7 (burglary); Person Felony, severity level 4 (aggravated burglary — occupied dwelling)
elements: Defendant, without authority, entered into or remained within any building or structure
With intent to commit a felony, theft, or sexually motivated crime therein
enhancements: Occupied dwelling (Aggravated Burglary — Person Felony severity level 4)
notes: Burglary of a non-dwelling is severity level 7. Burglary of a dwelling is also level 7. Aggravated burglary (occupied dwelling) is severity level 4 person felony. Kansas no longer requires 'breaking' — unauthorized entry is sufficient.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 4
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — typically 38-172 months depending on criminal history
elements: Defendant, without authority, entered into or remained within an occupied dwelling
With intent to commit a felony, theft, or sexually motivated crime
While a person was present
notes: Aggravated burglary of an occupied dwelling is one of the most serious property crimes. Severity level 4 person felony — same as aggravated battery with a deadly weapon.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 9 ($1,500-$24,999); higher levels for more valuable vehicles
elements: Defendant obtained or exerted unauthorized control over a motor vehicle of another
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Motor vehicle theft follows the general theft statute. Most vehicles exceed the $1,500 felony threshold. Joyriding without intent to deprive permanently is a lesser offense.

offense_class: Same as theft based on value
elements: Defendant obtained control over stolen property
Knowing the property to be stolen
notes: Receiving stolen property is included within Kansas's unified theft statute. Knowledge that property was stolen is required.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (under $1,500); Nonperson Felony, severity level 9 ($1,500+)
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged, destroyed, or substantially impaired the use of property
Without the owner's consent
notes: Kansas calls vandalism 'criminal damage to property.' Felony threshold matches theft at $1,500. Restitution typically ordered.

offense_class: Class B Nonperson Misdemeanor; Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor (dwelling or occupied structure)
elements: Defendant entered or remained upon or in any land, structure, vehicle, aircraft, or watercraft
Without authorization or consent
After having been notified not to enter or to leave
enhancements: Trespass of a dwelling (Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor)
notes: Notice requirement — posted signs, fencing, or actual notice. Trespass on agricultural land requires 'no trespass' signage or personal notice.

offense_class: Same as vandalism entry
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged, destroyed, or substantially impaired the use of property
Without the owner's consent
notes: Criminal damage to property is Kansas's statutory term for criminal mischief/vandalism. Same statute as the vandalism entry.

offense_class: Class B Person Misdemeanor (first); Class A Person Misdemeanor (second); Person Felony severity level 7 (third+)
elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused bodily harm to a family or household member
Or caused physical contact with a family or household member in a rude, insulting, or angry manner
mandatory_minimum: 48 hours (first); 90 days (second); per guidelines (third+ as felony)
enhancements: Second conviction within 5 years (Class A Person Misdemeanor with 90-day mandatory)
Third or subsequent conviction (Person Felony severity level 7)
notes: Kansas has a dedicated domestic battery statute. Mandatory arrest for probable cause. 48-hour mandatory minimum on first offense. Third offense is a felony. Batterer intervention program typically ordered.

offense_class: Class B Person Misdemeanor (first); escalating with priors
elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused bodily harm
To a family or household member
Or caused physical contact in a rude, insulting, or angry manner
enhancements: Second within 5 years (Class A with 90-day mandatory)
Third or subsequent (Person Felony severity level 7)
notes: Same statute as domestic violence entry. Federal firearms prohibition applies upon conviction. 'Family or household member' includes spouses, former spouses, persons who have been in a dating relationship, co-parents, and cohabitants.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 9 (knowing endangerment); Class A Person Misdemeanor (reckless endangerment)
elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused or permitted a child under 18 to be in a situation
In which the child's life, body, or health was injured or endangered
enhancements: Resulting in great bodily harm or death
notes: Knowing endangerment is a felony; reckless endangerment is a misdemeanor. Includes leaving children in hot cars, drug exposure, and other negligent supervision.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — typically 31-136 months with criminal history
elements: Defendant knowingly tortured, cruelly beat, or inflicted cruel and inhuman corporal punishment upon a child under 18
Or shook, kicked, burned, or cut a child under 18 in a manner likely to cause bodily harm
notes: Kansas child abuse statute specifically enumerates prohibited acts. Severity level 5 person felony — serious charge affecting future criminal history scoring. DCF investigation accompanies criminal charges.

offense_class: Class A Person Misdemeanor (first); Person Felony severity level 6 (second+ within 5 years)
elements: A protection from abuse or stalking order was issued
Defendant knowingly violated the order
enhancements: Second or subsequent violation within 5 years (Person Felony severity level 6)
notes: First violation is a person misdemeanor. Second within 5 years becomes a person felony. Contact through third parties can constitute a violation.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 7 (first); Person Felony, severity level 5 (second+)
elements: Defendant intentionally engaged in a course of conduct targeted at a specific person
That would cause a reasonable person to feel fear
notes: Stalking is a person felony even for first offense. 'Course of conduct' requires two or more acts. Cyberstalking is included.

offense_class: Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant, with intent to harass, intimidate, or annoy another
Made a phone call, sent electronic communication, or caused contact to be made
Without legitimate purpose
notes: Covers unwanted phone calls, texts, emails, and social media contact. Must be without legitimate purpose and intended to harass.

statute_title: Mistreatment of an Elder Person or Dependent Adult
offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5 (knowing infliction of harm); Class A Person Misdemeanor (unreasonable treatment)
elements: Defendant knowingly committed an act against a person 60 or older, or an adult with a disability
That was unjustifiable physical pain or the taking of financial resources
notes: Kansas has a specific elder/dependent adult mistreatment statute. Covers physical abuse, neglect, and financial exploitation. Adult Protective Services investigates.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (general); Nonperson Felony severity level 9 (prohibited person)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
In a prohibited place or while a prohibited person
notes: Kansas enacted permitless carry in 2015. Criminal carrying now primarily applies to prohibited persons and carrying in restricted locations (government buildings, courthouses, etc.).

statute_title: Criminal Possession of a Firearm by a Convicted Felon
offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 8 (nonperson felony prior); Person Felony, severity level 8 (person felony prior)
elements: Defendant possessed a firearm
Defendant has been convicted of a person or nonperson felony
enhancements: Prior person felony makes this a person felony
notes: Kansas law prohibits firearm possession for 5-10 years after felony conviction depending on the felony type. Drug felony = 5 years. Person felony = 10 years or lifetime for certain offenses.

statute_title: Criminal Carrying — Prohibited Person or Location
offense_class: Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor; Nonperson Felony (prohibited person)
elements: Defendant carried a concealed weapon
In a location prohibited by law or while a prohibited person
notes: With Kansas's 2015 permitless carry law, this applies primarily to restricted locations and prohibited persons. Persons under 21 cannot carry concealed handguns.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 6 (at occupied dwelling/vehicle); Nonperson Felony, severity level 8 (at unoccupied building)
elements: Defendant recklessly discharged a firearm
At an occupied dwelling, building, or vehicle
enhancements: Occupied dwelling or vehicle (Person Felony severity level 6)
notes: Kansas has a specific criminal discharge statute. Shooting at an occupied dwelling is a severity level 6 person felony — very serious charge.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 8 (first, under $100,000); severity level 5 ($100,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly and with intent to defraud
Obtained, possessed, transferred, used, or attempted to use the personal identifying information of another
For economic benefit or to harm another
notes: Kansas's identity theft statute covers use of names, SSNs, dates of birth, and other personal identifiers. Restitution typically ordered.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant had lawful possession of property
Defendant obtained or exerted unauthorized control over the property
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Embezzlement is charged under the unified theft statute. The distinguishing element is lawful initial possession. Common in employee, fiduciary, and public official contexts.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 8 (negotiable/government); Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor (other)
elements: Defendant, with intent to defraud
Made, altered, or endorsed a written instrument purporting to be the act of another
Or falsely made or altered a written instrument
notes: Forgery of checks, currency, and government documents is a felony. Other forgery is a misdemeanor. Uttering a forged document is included.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 8
elements: Defendant made, altered, or possessed counterfeit currency or government instruments
With intent to defraud
notes: Primarily a federal crime. State charges may be filed under Kansas forgery statute. Relatively rare at the state level.

offense_class: Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor (under $1,500); Nonperson Felony, severity level 9 ($1,500+)
elements: Defendant made, issued, or drew a check
Knowing at the time there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Kansas has a separate worthless check statute. Dishonor notice triggers presumption of intent if not made good within 7 days.

statute_title: Insurance Fraud — Making a False Claim
offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 7 ($25,000+); severity level 9 (under $25,000)
elements: Defendant knowingly presented or caused to be presented a false or fraudulent insurance claim
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: Kansas Insurance Department investigates. Restitution and civil penalties apply in addition to criminal penalties.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 9 (under $25,000); severity level 7 ($25,000+)
elements: Defendant used a credit card knowing it was stolen, forged, expired, or revoked
Or used another person's credit card without authorization
To obtain money, goods, or services
notes: Kansas has a specific credit card fraud statute. May also be charged as identity theft or theft.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 7 ($100,000+); severity level 9 (under $100,000)
elements: Defendant knowingly conducted a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of criminal activity
With intent to promote criminal activity or conceal the source/nature of the proceeds
notes: Kansas money laundering statute applies to proceeds from any felony. Forfeiture provisions also apply.

offense_class: Same as theft by value
elements: Defendant obtained control over property by deception
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: General fraud is charged as theft by deception under Kansas's unified theft statute. Covers false representations, promises, and schemes to defraud.

offense_class: Class A Person Misdemeanor (first); Person Felony severity level 9 (second+)
elements: Defendant intentionally touched the intimate parts of another person
Without consent
Done for the purpose of arousing or satisfying the sexual desires of either party
enhancements: Second or subsequent offense (Person Felony severity level 9)
notes: Sexual battery is Kansas's term for sexual assault not involving penetration. First offense is a person misdemeanor. Sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Off-grid Person Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly engaged in sexual intercourse with another person
Who did not consent, when the victim was overcome by force or fear
Or was unconscious or physically incapacitated
Or was incapable of giving consent due to mental deficiency or disease
mandatory_minimum: Hard 25 — 25 years minimum before parole eligibility (Jessica's Law for child victims)
notes: Rape in Kansas is an off-grid person felony. Jessica's Law mandates Hard 25 for rape of a child under 14. Sex offender registration is lifetime. Kansas defines rape as nonconsensual sexual intercourse.

offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (first); Class A Misdemeanor (second); Person Felony severity level 9 (third+)
elements: Defendant intentionally exposed a sex organ or engaged in sexual intercourse, lewd fondling, or touching
In the presence of another person who was not consenting
Done with intent to arouse or gratify sexual desires
enhancements: Third or subsequent (Person Felony severity level 9)
notes: Kansas uses 'lewd and lascivious behavior.' First offense is a Class B Misdemeanor. Third offense becomes a person felony with sex offender registration.

statute_title: Selling Sexual Relations / Buying Sexual Relations
offense_class: Class B Misdemeanor (selling, first); Class A Misdemeanor (buying); Person Felony severity level 9 (buying, if victim under 18)
penalty_max: 6 months (Class B); 1 year (Class A); per guidelines (felony)
elements: Defendant performed or offered to perform sexual intercourse or sodomy for money
Or hired or offered to hire a person for sexual intercourse or sodomy
notes: Kansas treats buying as more serious than selling. Buying from a minor under 18 is a person felony. Promoting prostitution (pimping) is separately charged under § 21-6420.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5 (possession); Off-grid (production)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed material depicting a child under 18 engaged in sexually explicit conduct
Or produced, promoted, or distributed such material
mandatory_minimum: Hard 25 for production involving child under 14
notes: Possession is severity level 5. Production is off-grid. Each image/video is a separate count. Lifetime sex offender registration required.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5
penalty_max: Per sentencing guidelines — typically 31-136 months with criminal history
elements: Defendant is required to register under the Kansas Offender Registration Act
Defendant knowingly failed to register, verify, or update registration
notes: Failure to register is a severity level 5 person felony — very serious charge in Kansas. Must register within 3 business days of any change.

statute_title: Indecent Liberties with a Child / Unlawful Sexual Relations
offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 5 (indecent liberties, 14-15); Off-grid Person Felony (aggravated, under 14)
penalty_max: Per guidelines (severity level 5); Life with Hard 25 (under 14)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual intercourse or lewd fondling with a child
Who was 14 or 15 years of age and the defendant was 4+ years older
Or the child was under 14
notes: Kansas's age of consent is 16. Indecent liberties with a child applies when victim is 14-15 and defendant is 4+ years older. Aggravated indecent liberties (under 14) triggers Jessica's Law Hard 25.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant engaged in brawling or fighting
Or disturbed an assembly or meeting
Or used offensive, obscene, or abusive language calculated to provoke a breach of the peace
notes: Class C Misdemeanor — the lowest level in Kansas. Common charge for minor public disturbances.

offense_class: Class A Misdemeanor (obstruction); Person Felony severity level 9 (physical interference with officer)
elements: Defendant knowingly obstructed, resisted, or opposed a person authorized to serve legal process or maintain public order
While the person was performing a lawful duty
enhancements: Physical interference with a law enforcement officer (Person Felony severity level 9)
notes: Obstruction is a misdemeanor. Physical interference with a law enforcement officer is a person felony. Kansas distinguishes between passive resistance and active physical interference.

statute_title: Obstruction of Justice / Obstructing Legal Process
offense_class: Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor (general); Person Felony severity level 9 (witness intimidation)
elements: Defendant knowingly and willfully obstructed, hindered, or delayed the enforcement of law
Or destroyed, altered, or concealed evidence
Or induced a witness to withhold testimony
notes: Separate from interference with law enforcement. Covers evidence tampering, witness intimidation, and obstruction of legal proceedings.

offense_class: Court-imposed sanctions
penalty_max: 6 months for criminal contempt; civil contempt until compliance
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a court order
Or disrupted court proceedings
Or engaged in conduct disrespectful to the court
notes: Kansas distinguishes direct contempt (in court's presence) from indirect contempt (outside court). Summary punishment available for direct contempt. Due process hearing required for indirect.

offense_class: Class C Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant consumed alcoholic liquor on public property or in a public place
Or possessed an open container of alcoholic liquor in a public place
notes: Kansas does not have a traditional 'public intoxication' statute. Instead, it criminalizes drinking in public/open container. Local ordinances may have additional provisions.

statute_title: Failure to Appear / Aggravated Failure to Appear
offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 9 (felony case); Class A Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case)
elements: Defendant was released on bond or recognizance
Defendant willfully failed to appear before any court as required
enhancements: Underlying felony case (Nonperson Felony severity level 9)
notes: Aggravated failure to appear (felony case) is a felony itself. Bond forfeiture and bench warrant issued. Consecutive sentence possible.

statute_title: Making a False Report / Filing a False Report
offense_class: Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor; Class B Person Misdemeanor (false alarm)
elements: Defendant knowingly gave a false alarm or report of a crime or emergency
Knowing the report to be false
notes: False police reports and false emergency calls. Swatting may be charged under this statute or as more serious offenses if harm results.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 9
elements: Defendant knowingly communicated a threat to commit violence
With intent to place another person in fear
Or to cause evacuation of a building, vehicle, or place of assembly
notes: Criminal threat is a person felony in Kansas, even for first offense. Covers bomb threats, death threats, and threats to cause serious harm.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 7
elements: Defendant knowingly made a false statement under oath
Material to the issue or matter of inquiry
In any proceeding before a court, tribunal, or public body
notes: Perjury is a severity level 7 nonperson felony — serious charge. The statement must be material. Includes sworn testimony, affidavits, and depositions.

offense_class: Person Felony, severity level 7
elements: Defendant offered, gave, or promised anything of value to a public official
With intent to influence the official's act, vote, opinion, or judgment
notes: Bribery of a public official is a person felony. Both the giver and receiver can be charged. Includes bribery of witnesses and jurors.

offense_class: Nonperson Felony, severity level 8 (felony custody); Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor (misdemeanor custody)
elements: Defendant escaped from custody
While held in lawful custody on a criminal charge or conviction
notes: Escape charge level corresponds to custody level. Includes walking away from work release and community corrections. Aggravated escape (using force) carries higher severity.

offense_class: Class A Nonperson Misdemeanor (first); Nonperson Felony severity level 10 (second+)
elements: Defendant knowingly killed, injured, maimed, tortured, or cruelly beat an animal
Or abandoned or neglected an animal
notes: Kansas passed stronger animal cruelty laws in recent years. Second offense is a felony. Dogfighting and cockfighting have separate enhanced provisions.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — court may revoke probation and impose original sentence
penalty_max: Up to the maximum sentence for the original offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation must be established by a preponderance of the evidence
notes: Kansas uses a graduated sanctions system for probation violations. Quick-dip jail sanctions (2-3 day increments) before full revocation. Court must make findings on the record.

offense_class: Not a new criminal charge — Kansas Prisoner Review Board determines consequences
penalty_max: Return to incarceration — up to remainder of sentence
elements: Defendant was released on postrelease supervision
Defendant violated a condition of supervision
notes: Kansas uses 'postrelease supervision' rather than 'parole.' Kansas Prisoner Review Board conducts revocation hearings. Graduated sanctions apply. New criminal charges may also be filed.

offense_class: Same as the underlying offense
elements: Defendant intentionally aided, abetted, advised, hired, counseled, or procured another to commit a crime
notes: An aider is equally liable with the principal. Mere association or presence is insufficient — must show intentional assistance. Applies to all Kansas crimes.

offense_class: Generally one severity level below the completed offense on the sentencing grid
penalty_max: One severity level below the completed offense
elements: Defendant performed an overt act toward the commission of a crime
With the intent to commit the crime
The act was more than mere preparation
notes: Attempt is graded one severity level below the completed offense. Exception: attempted first-degree murder is off-grid. Renunciation may be a defense if complete and voluntary.

offense_class: Generally one severity level below the target offense
penalty_max: One severity level below the target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with another person to commit a crime
With the intent to promote or facilitate the commission of the crime
One or more parties performed an overt act in furtherance of the agreement
notes: Conspiracy requires an agreement, intent, and an overt act. Conspiracy to commit an off-grid offense may itself be an off-grid offense. Withdrawal is a defense if timely.
